goal.source_text: More downforce without going over 15 N of drag at 25 m/s. You can change the angle, span, flap angle, flap size and endplates. Keep the chord.
assumptions: Chord, airfoil, mounts and ride height stay fixed.

design_space.name: FSAE-style rear wing

parameters.name: chord_mm
parameters.description: Total chord, main element plus flap

parameters.name: flap_chord_frac
parameters.description: Flap chord as a fraction of total chord

notes: Ranges from PLAN.md B.5; W-B owns the real solver and may narrow them before CP-B.

metric_catalog.name: downforce_n
metric_catalog.description: Downforce at the design speed (VLM + viscous correction + endplates)

metric_catalog.name: drag_n
metric_catalog.description: Total drag: induced + section profile + endplate friction

metric_catalog.name: drag_profile_n
metric_catalog.description: Section profile drag (NeuralFoil) plus endplate skin friction

metric_catalog.name: cl
metric_catalog.description: Wing lift coefficient on planform area

metric_catalog.name: stall_margin_deg
metric_catalog.description: Section stall angle minus angle of attack (negative = stalled)

metric_catalog.name: span_efficiency
metric_catalog.description: Oswald e from Prandtl lifting-line theory for the planform

payload.explanation: Increasing span 850→1000 mm raised downforce 19.6% and drag 11.0%, stall margin unchanged. Downforce and stall predictions matched; drag overshot because profile drag rose 19.3% more than anticipated. Induced drag rose 8.8% while L/D improved 7.7%, confirming efficient span addition.
payload.lesson: Span increases add downforce efficiently but profile drag can rise more than expected.

beliefs.text: Span increases add downforce efficiently but profile drag can rise more than expected.

payload.rationale: Endplates raise effective aspect ratio, cutting induced drag at a small profile-drag cost, so increasing height from 200 mm should add a little downforce and reduce drag, easing the drag limit.

payload.explanation: Endplate height increased effective aspect ratio by 13.8%, cutting induced drag 8.28% while profile drag rose 12.6%. Downforce gained 2.15%, total drag fell 3.58%, so L/D improved 5.94%. Predictions were directionally correct, but profile drag increase was above the 5-10% predicted range, making L/D exceed 5%.
payload.lesson: Endplate height gains lift and cuts induced drag, but profile drag rises more than expected.

payload.explanation: Increasing flap chord fraction from 0.3 to 0.35 produced only 0.403% more downforce, far below predicted 4-12%. Drag rose 4.38%, in predicted range, mostly profile drag +13.69%; induced drag +0.808%. Stall margin unchanged at 2.0 deg. Verdict accepted: gain small but positive, within drag margin.
payload.lesson: Larger flap chord mostly adds profile drag, not downforce, when flap is already near its effective limit.

payload.explanation: The design reduced flap 15→10° and raised AoA 7.5→8.5°. Actual: downforce −3.69%, drag −14.3% (profile drag −30.7%, induced −7.25%), stall margin +25.0%. Predictions missed direction. Flap reduction lowered camber more than AoA raise increased lift, unloading section: less lift and profile drag, later stall.
payload.lesson: Reducing flap at high AoA cuts lift/drag and raises stall margin; AoA increase can't compensate.
